subject: Prompt handoff & verification plan for FastRetail performance qualification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Hi Elaine / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance qualification side so we have alignment before we touch the harness: 

- SLO targets we heard from you: p95 latency ~200ms for short queries (<=64 tokens), streaming first-byte <=50ms where applicable, and peak concurrency target ~1,000 RPS. Please correct if I misremembered any number.
- We will run a two-stage qualification: 1) reproducibility harness (single-run bench to validate measurement definitions) and 2) extended soak (24–72h) for stability and thermal behavior.
- Measurement definitions we suggest (details below): p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency (client->last-token), first-byte latency for streaming, per-request token rate, and tail latencies with cold/warm-start separation.
- Prompt handoff: please share a representative prompt bundle (masked PII) and an expected-output set or acceptance criteria for generative quality checks. A JSONL with prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior notes works best.

Attached: benchmark-template.csv (simple CSV to map prompt_id -> expected_len / concurrency weight / sequence length class).

Can you share: (a) the prompt bundle, (b) any internal pass/fail rules for quality that should be applied during the qualification, and (c) preferred time window for the soak run?

I'll loop in our solutions lead (Kimberly) after we sync on the harness details. If you'd like, we can schedule a short 30-minute check-in Wednesday to walk the Drive artifacts together.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (555) 213-0098

From: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Thanks Ben — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and material we've attached to get you started:

- Confirming SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for short queries (<=64 tokens); for medium queries (65–256 tokens) p95 <= 350ms. Streaming first-byte <= 50ms on average, and we want to keep streaming rebuffer events <1% over a 24h window. Peak concurrency target is 1,000 RPS but please also include a 200 RPS baseline run.
- Prompt bundle: attached (retail-prompt-bundle.jsonl) — each line is prompt_id, prompt_text, and a small annotation field. We redacted full user PII.
- Quality checks: we have a lightweight callable test that asserts presence of key slot tokens (e.g., product_name, price_range) and a manual review sample of 50 generations for QA.
- Soak window: target week of Jan 25, prefer Tues/Wed morning PST for setup.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0FastRetailPromptsExample
Attachments: retail-prompt-bundle.jsonl

Best,
Elaine Gomez
Head of ML Ops, FastRetail
elaine@fastretail.io
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Thanks Elaine — received the bundle and drive link, appreciate the annotations. Quick note on how we'll run the reproducibility harness and what we need from your side: 

- Harness: we'll run our benchmark harness (open-source wrapper + Redwood runner) to generate stable traffic patterns. The harness will: 1) run short/medium/long prompt mixes, 2) simulate streaming when marked in prompt metadata, 3) capture token-level timestamps and per-request traces.
- Repro steps (short): we need the JSONL prompt bundle, a seeds.csv with random seeds for deterministic RNG (we'll provide a template), and the mapping CSV (attached earlier). We'll publish the exact harness command and environment (Docker image + commit hash) for you to reproduce locally.
- Determinism: for quality regression checks, we'll use fixed temperature/decoding settings and record model_rng_seed. If you require non-deterministic sampling for production-like behavior, we'll add a repeatable sampling seed history to the logs so outputs can be correlated.
- Pass criteria suggestion: latency SLOs (p95) met under 95% of runs AND quality acceptance on >90% of sampled prompts. We can make thresholds configurable.

Kimberly, can you add the specific model-variant matrix we should include (quantized vs full-fp) and any recommended batch/concurrency knobs?

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Hi Elaine / Ben — adding the measurement-spec detail so there is no ambiguity on how we report numbers. High-level items included below; full draft attached (measurement-spec.md).

- Models to include: open-llm-v1 (float16), open-llm-v1-quant (int8), and a fallback smaller model (open-llm-compact) for cost tradeoffs. We'll label them in the report as v1-fp16, v1-int8, v1-compact.
- Batching: continuous batching on production runner with a dynamic batch cap set to 64 tokens / request or 128 depending on seq-len profile. For the reproduce-run we will run both conservative (batch cap 32) and aggressive (batch cap 128) settings.
- Warm-up: we recommend a 10-minute warm-up before measurements, and separate cold-start tests (single request after idle >30m).
- Latency definitions:
  * first_byte_latency: time from request start to first token byte returned (for streaming).
  * last_token_latency: time from request start to final token completion (end-to-end).
  * tail latency: p95/p99 computed on last_token_latency across the run window after warm-up.
- Logging: required fields per request -> request_id, prompt_id, model_variant, seed, first_byte_ts, last_token_ts, num_tokens, batch_size, instance_id, and trace_id. We'll provide a logging schema.

Attachment: measurement-spec.md (markdown stub)

I'll schedule a short dry-run with our infra team the week prior to the soak. Tentatively planning Jan 24 for the dry-run if that works with your calendar.

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.io>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Great — two quick questions before the dry-run: 

1) Streaming reproducibility: we need to simulate real-world client behavior where tokens may be consumed by downstream UI at variable rates and network RTTs vary. Can the harness introduce token-level jitter and client-side consumption pacing? We want to ensure rebuffering metrics are realistic.

2) Logs / evidence for security/compliance: our audit team will need request traces and anonymized payloads for the run. What retention and redaction options do you offer for the logs generated during the soak?

Attached: retail-prompt-bundle.jsonl (we added a few more examples).

Thanks — we can do the dry-run Jan 24 morning PST.

Elaine
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Gomez <elaine@fastretail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 07:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt handoff & verification plan

Perfect — thanks for the questions, Elaine. Quick answers and agreed next steps below: 

- Streaming jitter: yes. Our harness can inject client-side consumption patterns and network latency distributions (we use a pluggable module for jitter profiles). For the dry-run we'll run two profiles: (A) steady consumption (production-like) and (B) bursty mobile clients (high jitter). We'll include rebuffer and dropped-frame style metrics as part of the report.
- Logs/retention/redaction: we can provide anonymized request logs (request_id, prompt_id, model_variant, timestamps) and a redacted payload export (masking tokens that match PII regex). Retention for the qualification run is configurable — default 30 days; we can extend retention to 90 days on request. All logs will be delivered through a secure S3 bucket with limited ACLs.

Action items / owners: 
- Ben: publish harness command, seeds.csv template, and a short runbook by EOD Mon (Jan 18).
- Marissa: finalize measurement-spec.md and logging schema by Jan 20.
- Elaine / FastRetail: confirm final prompt bundle and pass/fail rules by Jan 21.
- Dry-run: Jan 24 morning PST (engineering + infra call) — invite will follow.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0FastRetailPromptsExample, HubSpot: 34567

If that looks good I'll raise the HubSpot tasks and send the calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Ben
